Key architectural components include a zero-build frontend workflow, server-side engineering and dual-mass constraint validations, and a deterministic six-phase mission simulation driven by a seeded random generator.

details:
Mission Forge is an offline-first spaceflight simulator built on a monolithic two-tier software stack. A Python FastAPI server handles REST APIs and static files, while all missions, rockets, and components reside in local JSON files loaded into app memory at startup rather than a database. The frontend relies on vanilla ES6 modules, a hash router, and a centralized pub/sub state store with a completely zero-build workflow.

All authoritative engineering calculations execute strictly server-side. This incorporates dual-mass validation—enforcing both destination payload capacity and mission maximum mass constraints via an effective mass limit—alongside rigorous power, budget, capability, and deduplicated compatibility checks.

For execution, the app runs a deterministic, six-phase simulation from launch to completion governed by a seeded random generator, ensuring entirely reproducible telemetry and events. Final outcomes are evaluated through a comprehensive 100-point scoring system mapped directly to formal letter grades.

Visual rendering features an integrated Three.js scene utilizing procedural geometries or optional custom Blender models. To ensure absolute offline reliability during demonstrations, it implements a robust three-tier loading strategy: CDN primary, a local bundle fallback, and a graceful text fallback. Finally, all data catalogs are thoroughly grounded in published official specifications from agencies like NASA and SpaceX via strict field-level specification verification.
